items.q: Crops that are sown in the winter season (October to December) and harvested in spring are called:
Which of the following is a kharif crop?
Loosening and turning of the soil before sowing seeds is called:
Which of the following is a manure and not a chemical fertiliser?
Why do farmers grow a leguminous crop such as gram or peas in a field after a cereal crop?
items.proposedAnswer: Leguminous plants have Rhizobium bacteria in their root nodules. These bacteria fix nitrogen from the air and add nitrogen compounds to the soil, so the soil becomes richer for the next crop.
keyPoints: Roots of legumes have Rhizobium bacteria

items.q: A farmer has sandy soil, very little water and an orchard of fruit trees. Which method of irrigation would save the most water for her?
options: Flooding the field from a canal

items.q: A farmer stores harvested wheat in a sack without drying it properly. What is the most likely result?
options: Moisture lets fungi and pests grow and spoil the grain
The grain slowly turns into manure
The grain becomes richer in nutrients
The grain gets converted into seeds of a new variety

items.q: Why is the excessive use of chemical fertilisers harmful to the environment?
items.proposedAnswer: Excess fertilisers reduce soil fertility over time and are washed into ponds and rivers, where they cause pollution and harm water life. They can also contaminate drinking water.
keyPoints: Reduces soil fertility in the long run
Washed into water bodies and pollutes them

items.q: Which of the following is a fungus?
Malaria is spread by:
Rhizobium bacteria are useful to farmers because they:
options: Fix atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes

items.q: Dough used for making bread rises because:
options: Yeast kills bacteria in the flour
Yeast respires and releases bubbles of carbon dioxide

items.q: How does adding a large amount of salt help in preserving pickles and fish?
items.proposedAnswer: Salt removes moisture from the food and from any microorganisms that land on it, so they cannot grow. This keeps the food from spoiling for a long time.

items.q: A person with influenza, which is caused by a virus, takes an antibiotic. What is true about this treatment?
options: It will not work because antibiotics act against bacteria and not viruses
It will kill the virus within a day
It works better than any other medicine for viruses
It will turn the virus into a harmless bacterium

items.q: In pasteurisation, milk is heated and then chilled quickly. Why is it chilled quickly?
options: To increase the amount of cream
To prevent any surviving microorganisms from multiplying
To add vitamin D to it

items.q: Why should a patient take an antibiotic only on a doctor's advice and complete the full course?
items.proposedAnswer: The doctor knows the right type and dose for the infection. If the dose is too small or the course is stopped early, the bacteria may survive, and the medicine may become less effective on them in future. Unnecessary antibiotics can also harm useful bacteria in the body.
keyPoints: Right medicine and dose for the infection
Wrong use makes antibiotics less effective later

items.q: Which of the following was the first fully synthetic fibre?
Rayon, made from wood pulp, is also called:
Which of the following is a thermosetting plastic?
Handles of electrical switches are made from Bakelite because it:
options: Is a good conductor of electricity
Is a poor conductor of heat and electricity

items.q: What is the difference between thermoplastics and thermosetting plastics? Give one example of each.
items.proposedAnswer: Thermoplastics soften on heating and can be reshaped again and again, for example polythene. Thermosetting plastics harden once moulded and cannot be softened by heating, for example Bakelite.
keyPoints: Thermoplastics can be softened and reshaped
Thermosetting plastics cannot be softened again

items.q: Why is a layer of Teflon applied on the surface of non-stick frying pans?
options: It is a good conductor so food cooks faster
It is very slippery, so food does not stick to it
It reacts with the food and flavours it

items.q: Plastic bags thrown away in a field remain there for many years. This is because:
options: Plastic dissolves in soil to form humus
Microorganisms cannot break down most plastics, so they are non-biodegradable

items.q: Why is it not advised to wear clothes made of nylon or polyester while working near a flame in the kitchen?
items.proposedAnswer: Synthetic fibres catch fire easily and melt when heated. The molten fibre sticks to the skin and causes severe burns.
keyPoints: Melted fibre sticks to skin and burns

items.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
Which of the following is a non-metal?
The property of metals by which they can be drawn into wires is called:
Magnesium ribbon reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid and a gas is released. The gas is:
Give two reasons why metals are used for making cooking vessels.
items.proposedAnswer: Metals are good conductors of heat, so food cooks quickly. They also have high melting points and can be shaped into vessels because they are malleable.

items.q: Carbon dioxide dissolved in water turns blue litmus paper red. What does this show?
options: Carbon dioxide is a basic oxide
Carbon dioxide forms a neutral solution

items.q: An iron nail is dipped in blue copper sulphate solution. After some time a brownish coating forms on the nail and the blue colour fades. Why?
options: Copper displaces iron from the solution
More reactive iron displaces copper from the solution
Water in the solution turns into copper

items.q: Why are sodium and potassium stored in kerosene oil?
items.proposedAnswer: Sodium and potassium are very reactive metals. They react vigorously with oxygen and moisture of the air and can catch fire, so they are kept immersed in kerosene to keep air and water away.
keyPoints: React with oxygen and moisture, may catch fire
Kerosene keeps air and water away

items.q: Which of the following is a fossil fuel?
CNG stands for:
Which petroleum product is used for surfacing roads?
The process of separating the various constituents of petroleum is called:
How is coke obtained from coal and what is one use of coke?
items.proposedAnswer: Coke is obtained by heating coal strongly in the absence of air. It is a tough, porous, black substance that is almost pure carbon, and is used in making steel and in extracting many metals.
keyPoints: Coal heated in absence of air
Used in steel making or extraction of metals

items.q: Coal is called a non-renewable resource because:
options: It cannot be burnt a second time
It is found only in India
It took millions of years to form and cannot be replaced quickly

items.q: Why is CNG considered a cleaner fuel than petrol or diesel for vehicles?
options: It burns with much less harmful smoke and fewer pollutants
It does not burn at all
It produces no gas on burning

items.q: Why should we conserve petroleum and natural gas?
items.proposedAnswer: They took millions of years to form and their stocks are limited. Burning them also pollutes the air, so we should use them carefully and look for other sources of energy.
keyPoints: Took millions of years to form

items.q: The process of burning a substance in air to give out heat is called:
Which zone of a candle flame is the hottest?
Which of the following sets of three are necessary for a fire to start and continue?
Which fire extinguisher is best for a fire caused by electrical equipment?
What is meant by ignition temperature? Give one example of how it matters in daily life.
items.proposedAnswer: Ignition temperature is the lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire. For example, white phosphorus has a very low ignition temperature, so it is kept under water.
keyPoints: Lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire
Example such as white phosphorus kept under water

items.q: Why is water not used to put out a fire caused by burning oil?
options: Oil is lighter than water, floats on it and keeps burning
Water reacts with oil to make more fuel
Water is lighter than oil, so it floats away
Water has a very high ignition temperature

items.q: A burning candle is covered with an upside-down glass jar and it goes out after some time. The reason is that:
options: The glass makes the wax cold
The oxygen inside the jar is used up
The jar contains too much oxygen

items.q: Why does a paper cup holding water not catch fire when it is heated over a flame?
items.proposedAnswer: The water absorbs the heat from the paper, so the paper stays below its ignition temperature and does not burn.
keyPoints: Paper stays below its ignition temperature
So it does not catch fire

items.q: The record of endangered species of plants and animals is kept in the:
Deforestation means:
options: Clearing of forests on a large scale

items.q: A species that is found only in a particular area and nowhere else is called:
What is a biosphere reserve? Name one biosphere reserve in India.
items.proposedAnswer: A biosphere reserve is a large protected area set aside to conserve the biodiversity of its plants and animals, and often the way of life of the people living there. One example is the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.
keyPoints: Conserves plants, animals and their habitat

items.q: Reforestation means:
options: Restocking destroyed forests by planting trees

items.q: A highway built through a forest area is most likely to harm wild animals because:
options: It breaks up their habitat and blocks their movement
It increases the number of trees

items.q: Explain how deforestation can lead to soil erosion and rise in temperature.
items.proposedAnswer: Roots of trees bind the soil, so without trees the soil is easily washed or blown away. Fewer trees also absorb less carbon dioxide and give less shade and rain, so the surroundings become hotter and drier.
keyPoints: Roots hold soil, so soil erodes
Less rain and shade, so more heat

items.q: The basic structural and functional unit of life is the:
Who first observed and named cells while looking at a thin slice of cork?
The part of a cell that contains the chromosomes carrying genes is the:
Write two differences between a plant cell and an animal cell.
items.proposedAnswer: A plant cell has a cell wall outside the cell membrane, but an animal cell does not. A plant cell has chloroplasts and usually a large central vacuole, while an animal cell has no chloroplasts and only small vacuoles.
keyPoints: Cell wall present only in plant cells
Plant cells have a large vacuole

items.q: The organelle in which photosynthesis takes place is the:
Which of the following cells would you expect to have the most chloroplasts?
options: A cell of a green leaf
A root cell inside the soil
A cell of the onion bulb

items.q: Why do plant cells have a cell wall while animal cells do not need one?
items.proposedAnswer: The cell wall gives plant cells shape, strength and protection. Plants have no skeleton, so the rigid wall helps them stay upright, while animals get support from skeletons and muscles.
keyPoints: Cell wall gives shape and strength
Animals are supported by other body parts

items.q: The fusion of a male gamete and a female gamete is called:
The male gamete is called the:
Which of the following reproduces by budding?
Differentiate between internal and external fertilisation. Give one example of each.
items.proposedAnswer: In internal fertilisation the sperm and egg join inside the body of the female, for example in humans or hens. In external fertilisation they join outside the body, in water, for example in frogs and fish.
keyPoints: External: outside body, usually in water
Examples such as hen and frog

items.q: Which of the following is a viviparous animal?
A frog lays hundreds of eggs but a hen lays only a few. Which reason explains this best?
options: Frog eggs are fertilised and develop in open water, where many eggs are eaten or lost, so more eggs improve survival chances
Hens do not need eggs to reproduce
Frog eggs are fertilised inside the female

items.q: Describe the changes in the life of a frog from egg to adult.
items.proposedAnswer: The fertilised egg develops into a tadpole that has a tail and gills and lives in water. The tadpole slowly grows legs, loses the tail and gills and develops lungs, becoming an adult frog. This change in form is called metamorphosis.
keyPoints: Egg develops into tadpole with gills and tail

items.q: The period of life roughly between the ages of 11 and 19 years is called:
The male sex hormone produced by the testes is:
The gland that controls the working of other endocrine glands and is often called the master gland is the:
What is the Adam's apple and why does it become visible in adolescent boys?
items.proposedAnswer: The Adam's apple is the visible bulge at the front of the neck. During adolescence the voice box (larynx) grows larger in boys, so it sticks out and the voice becomes deeper.
keyPoints: It is the enlarged voice box (larynx)
Seen as a bulge in the neck

items.q: Lack of iodine in the diet can cause a swelling of the neck called:
The sex of a human baby is decided by:
options: The X chromosome in the mother's egg
The X or Y chromosome carried by the father's sperm
The hormones of both parents at birth

items.q: Why do adolescents need a balanced diet and regular exercise?
items.proposedAnswer: Adolescents grow fast and need more proteins, vitamins and minerals for their growing body. Regular exercise keeps the body fit and healthy and helps the mind.
keyPoints: Balanced diet gives proteins, vitamins and minerals

items.q: The SI unit of force is the:

The force of friction always acts:
options: In the direction opposite to the motion
In the direction of the motion
At right angles to the surface only

items.q: Why are the soles of sports shoes made with grooves or a rough pattern?
items.proposedAnswer: Grooves increase friction between the shoe and the ground, so the player can grip the ground well and does not slip.

items.q: Which of the following is a non-contact force?
A sharp knife cuts a vegetable more easily than a blunt knife because:
options: With a smaller area of the edge, the same force gives a greater pressure

items.q: A camel can walk easily on soft sand without sinking. Explain why.
items.proposedAnswer: A camel has broad, flat feet. The broad area spreads its weight over a larger area, so the pressure on the sand is smaller and the feet do not sink.

items.q: Sound is produced when an object:
The unit in which frequency is measured is:
The loudness of a sound depends on the:
Why can sound not travel through a vacuum?
items.proposedAnswer: Sound needs a material medium such as air, water or a solid to travel. A vacuum has no particles that can vibrate and pass the sound on.

items.q: The range of frequencies audible to a normal human ear is about:
A girl's voice is usually thinner (higher pitched) than that of a grown man. The reason is:
options: Lower amplitude of her vocal cords
Her vocal cords vibrate at a lower frequency
Her vocal cords vibrate at a higher frequency

items.q: Suggest three ways in which noise pollution in a city can be reduced.
items.proposedAnswer: Noise can be reduced by switching off vehicle horns and engines when not needed, keeping the volume of music and TV low, and planting trees along roads. Using silencers on machines also helps.

items.q: Which of the following liquids conducts electricity?
Depositing a layer of a metal on another object using electric current is called:
When electric current passes through a conducting solution, it can cause:
How can you test whether a liquid is a good conductor of electricity?
items.proposedAnswer: Make a tester using a cell, a bulb or LED and two wires with free ends. Dip the free ends in the liquid. If the bulb glows or the LED lights up, the liquid conducts electricity.
keyPoints: Use a cell, bulb or LED and wires
Dip the wire ends in the liquid

items.q: In electroplating, the object to be plated is connected to:
options: The negative terminal of the battery
The positive terminal of the battery

items.q: Chromium plating is done on car parts and bicycle handlebars because chromium:
options: Is shiny, hard and does not corrode easily

items.q: Why should we not touch an electrical switch with wet hands?
items.proposedAnswer: Ordinary water contains dissolved salts, so it conducts electricity. Wet hands can let current pass through the body and cause an electric shock.
keyPoints: Ordinary water contains salts and conducts

items.q: According to the law of reflection, the angle of incidence is equal to the:

options: Virtual and upright, of the same size as the object

items.q: Which is the safest place to be during a thunderstorm?
Name the instrument used to record earthquake waves and the scale on which the strength of an earthquake is measured.
items.proposedAnswer: A seismograph records earthquake waves. The strength (magnitude) of an earthquake is measured on the Richter scale.

items.q: The splitting of white light into its seven colours is called:
The word AMBULANCE is written laterally inverted on the front of the vehicle. This is done so that:
options: The word can be read correctly in the rear-view mirror of the car ahead
The word is hidden from the driver

items.q: During a thunderstorm we see lightning first and hear thunder later. Why?
items.proposedAnswer: Light travels much faster than sound. The flash of lightning reaches our eyes almost instantly, while the sound of thunder takes longer to reach our ears.
keyPoints: Light is much faster than sound
Flash is seen almost at once

items.q: The process of separating the lighter husk (chaff) from the grain using the wind is called:
Cutting a mature crop from the field is called:
Which tool is used to sow seeds at a uniform distance and depth in the soil?
What is weeding and why is it necessary in a crop field?
items.proposedAnswer: Weeding is the removal of unwanted plants (weeds) that grow along with the crop. Weeds compete with the crop for water, nutrients, light and space, so removing them helps the crop grow well.
keyPoints: Weeds compete for water, nutrients and light

items.q: Which of the following is an advantage of manure over a chemical fertiliser?
options: It supplies nutrients faster and in a larger quantity
It contains more nutrients for each kilogram
It improves the texture of the soil and its ability to hold water by adding humus
It is easier to carry long distances

items.q: When seeds are put in water, damaged seeds float on the surface. This is because damaged seeds are:
Why are dried neem leaves often kept with stored grain in homes?
items.proposedAnswer: Neem leaves keep insects and pests away. This helps to protect the stored grains from damage and spoilage.
keyPoints: Neem leaves repel insects and pests

items.q: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
Which of the following is the smallest?
The conversion of sugar into alcohol by yeast is called:
What is a vaccine and how does it protect us from disease?
items.proposedAnswer: A vaccine contains weakened or dead disease-causing microbes. When it is given, the body makes antibodies against them, so if the real microbe attacks later, the body can fight it quickly.

items.q: Green fuzzy patches appear on a piece of bread kept in a warm and damp cupboard. They are most likely due to:
options: Dust that has settled on the bread
Fungal spores growing in warm, moist conditions

items.q: Which statement best explains how some bacteria help to keep the environment clean?
options: They make dead plants and animals last longer
They decompose dead plants and animals into simple substances

items.q: How can a housefly spread diseases like cholera? Suggest one precaution.
items.proposedAnswer: Houseflies sit on garbage and animal waste and pick up disease-causing microbes on their legs and bodies. When they sit on uncovered food they pass these microbes on. We should keep food covered and keep the surroundings clean.
keyPoints: Cover food and keep surroundings clean

items.q: Which of the following is a natural fibre?
Which synthetic fibre is often called artificial wool?
Terylene is a kind of:
Write any two properties of plastics that make them useful.
items.proposedAnswer: Plastics are light, strong and durable, and they are poor conductors of heat and electricity. They can also be moulded easily into many shapes and do not rust.
keyPoints: Poor conductors of heat and electricity

items.q: A mountaineer needs a rope that is strong, light and does not rot in water. Which fibre is the best choice?
Strong chemicals are often stored in plastic containers rather than metal ones because plastics:
options: Are generally non-reactive with many chemicals

items.q: Suggest three ways in which pollution from plastic can be reduced.
items.proposedAnswer: We can reduce the use of plastic bags by carrying cloth or jute bags, reuse plastic containers where safe, and send used plastic to be recycled. We should not throw plastic carelessly or burn it.

items.q: Which of the following metals is soft enough to be cut with a knife?
Which of the following non-metals is a good conductor of electricity?
Metals are said to be sonorous. This means they:
options: Can be cut with a knife
Produce a ringing sound when struck

items.q: A magnesium ribbon is burnt in air and the white ash is dissolved in water. What is the effect of this solution on red litmus paper, and why?
items.proposedAnswer: The ash is magnesium oxide, a metal oxide, and it dissolves in water to form a basic solution. It turns red litmus paper blue.

items.q: Gold and silver are used to make jewellery because they:
options: Are lustrous and do not corrode easily

items.q: For an iron nail to rust, which of the following are necessary?
Why are electric wires made of metal but covered with plastic?
items.proposedAnswer: The metal is a good conductor, so it carries electric current easily. Plastic is a poor conductor (an insulator), so it prevents shocks and short circuits.

items.q: The main constituent of natural gas is:
Petroleum is also commonly called:
Which of the following petroleum products is commonly used as fuel for domestic stoves and lamps?
Name any four products obtained from petroleum and give one use of each.
items.proposedAnswer: Petrol is used as a fuel in cars, diesel in trucks and buses, kerosene in stoves, and LPG for cooking. Paraffin wax is used for candles, lubricating oil in machines and bitumen for roads.

items.q: Which statement correctly differentiates coal from petroleum?
options: Coal formed from buried sea organisms and petroleum from forests
Coal formed from buried plants of ancient forests and petroleum from tiny sea organisms
Both formed in a few years

items.q: Burning coal in factories can lead to acid rain because:
options: Burning coal releases sulphur dioxide, which dissolves in rainwater

items.q: Explain in brief how petroleum was formed.
items.proposedAnswer: Millions of years ago, tiny sea plants and animals died and sank to the sea floor. They were covered by layers of sand and clay, and with heat and pressure over a very long time they changed into petroleum and natural gas.
keyPoints: Dead sea organisms settled on sea floor
Heat and pressure over millions of years

items.q: Which fuel is used in rockets because of its very high calorific value?
Which of the following is a non-combustible substance?
The calorific value of a fuel is expressed in:
What is spontaneous combustion? Give an example.
items.proposedAnswer: It is the type of combustion in which a substance suddenly catches fire on its own without any external flame or heat. White phosphorus catching fire in air at room temperature is an example.

items.q: A blanket is thrown over a person whose clothes have caught fire because it:
options: Cuts off the supply of air and cools the fire

items.q: The flame of a gas stove burns blue, whereas a candle flame is yellow. The blue flame indicates:
Why is it dangerous to burn coal in a closed room?
items.proposedAnswer: In a closed room the supply of oxygen is limited, so the coal undergoes incomplete combustion and gives out carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas. It can make people unconscious and can even kill them.

items.q: A protected area where wild animals are safe from hunting is called a:
Species that no longer exist on Earth are called:
The term fauna refers to:
One of the main reasons for deforestation is:
options: Clearing land for farming, housing and industries

items.q: What is an endangered species? Give one example.
items.proposedAnswer: An endangered species is a species of plant or animal whose numbers have fallen so low that it is in danger of becoming extinct. The tiger is an example.

items.q: Forests help to reduce floods because:
options: Roots of trees hold the soil and slow down the flow of rainwater
Forests increase the number of rivers

items.q: Which of the following actions would help the most to save a species from extinction?
options: Cutting the forest to build farms
Moving all its animals to one zoo
Banning hunting and protecting its habitat

items.q: Why do some birds travel long distances to other regions every year?
items.proposedAnswer: They migrate to escape harsh weather such as extreme cold, to find food, or to breed in a suitable place. Many return when the climate is favourable again.

items.q: The jelly-like substance that fills the cell and lies between the cell membrane and the nucleus is the:
Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
The part of the cell that controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell is the:
Which of the following is a unicellular organism?
What is the difference between unicellular and multicellular organisms? Give one example of each.
items.proposedAnswer: Unicellular organisms consist of a single cell that does all life functions, for example Amoeba. Multicellular organisms are made of many cells that are specialised for different functions, for example humans.
keyPoints: Examples such as Amoeba and humans

items.q: Nerve cells are long and branched. What is the most suitable reason?
options: Their shape helps them carry messages over long distances in the body
To make the body look attractive

items.q: Under a microscope, onion peel cells appear as regular, closely packed rectangles with thick outlines. The thick outline is due to the:
Why are cells called the building blocks of life?
items.proposedAnswer: Every living organism is made of one or more cells, just as a building is made of bricks. Cells group to form tissues, organs and organ systems, and each cell carries out life processes.
keyPoints: All organisms are made of cells

items.q: The female gametes (eggs) are produced in the:
In a human female, fertilisation takes place in the:
The developing human baby grows inside the:
In Amoeba, binary fission means that:
options: The cell splits into two daughter cells
A bud grows on its body
The cell joins with another cell

items.q: What is cloning? Name the first mammal cloned.
items.proposedAnswer: Cloning is the production of an exact copy of an organism that has the same genes as the original. The first mammal cloned successfully was a sheep named Dolly.

items.q: In the technique called IVF, the egg and sperm are made to join:
options: In a dish in the laboratory, and the embryo is then placed in the uterus

items.q: An unfertilised hen's egg bought from a shop will not hatch into a chick because:
options: There was no fusion of a sperm and an egg, so no zygote formed
It is kept in a cold room only

items.q: Frogs lay eggs in water, but hens lay eggs with a hard shell. Give a reason for each.
items.proposedAnswer: Frog eggs are fertilised outside the body and covered with jelly, and they need water to develop. A hen's egg is fertilised inside and has a hard shell that protects the developing chick on land.
keyPoints: Frog eggs need water and are covered by jelly
Hen's egg has a hard protective shell

items.q: The changes that occur at puberty are controlled by chemicals called:
The female sex hormone oestrogen is produced by the:
The menstrual cycle in a woman repeats about once every:
Which of the following is a secondary sexual character?
options: Growth of a beard in boys

items.q: What are hormones? Name two endocrine glands.
items.proposedAnswer: Hormones are chemical substances produced by endocrine glands that are carried by the blood to other parts of the body to control their working. Two endocrine glands are the pituitary gland and the thyroid gland.
keyPoints: Two glands such as pituitary and thyroid

items.q: A person has too much sugar in the blood because the pancreas does not make enough insulin. The disease is:
When a person is frightened, the adrenal glands release adrenaline. What is the effect?
options: It increases the heart rate and prepares the body to face the situation
It stops the heart for a moment

items.q: Why are hormones called chemical messengers?
items.proposedAnswer: Hormones are chemicals made in one part of the body, the endocrine gland, and carried by blood to another part, where they bring about a response. In this way they carry a message from one part to another.

items.q: Which of the following is a contact force?
A force can change:
options: The speed, direction or shape of an object

items.q: Which type of friction is the least?
Gas exerts pressure on the walls of its container because:
options: Gas particles keep colliding with the walls

items.q: State two ways of reducing friction.
items.proposedAnswer: Friction can be reduced by using lubricants such as oil or grease between moving parts, and by using ball bearings or wheels instead of sliding. Making surfaces smoother also reduces friction.

items.q: Pressure in water increases as we go deeper because:
options: There is more weight of water above
Air is heavier at the bottom

items.q: A heavy box is hard to start moving but easier to keep moving. The reason is that:
options: The box gets lighter after moving
The friction before motion starts is greater than sliding friction
The floor becomes smooth by itself

items.q: Why is the wall of a dam built thicker at the bottom than at the top?
items.proposedAnswer: The pressure of water increases with depth, so the bottom of the dam has to bear more pressure. A thicker wall at the bottom makes the dam strong enough to withstand this.

items.q: The number of vibrations of an object in one second is called its:

How is sound produced by the human voice box?
items.proposedAnswer: The voice box (larynx) contains two vocal cords stretched across it. When air from the lungs passes through, the vocal cords vibrate and produce sound.

items.q: Two astronauts walking on the Moon cannot talk to each other directly without radios because:
options: There is no air on the Moon, so sound cannot travel

items.q: Sound A has a frequency of 500 Hz and a small amplitude. Sound B has a frequency of 200 Hz and a large amplitude. Which statement is correct?
options: A is louder and has a lower pitch
A is louder and has a higher pitch
B has the higher pitch and is softer
A has the higher pitch and is softer

items.q: A rubber band is stretched and plucked. Why does its sound become shriller when it is stretched more tightly?
items.proposedAnswer: A tighter rubber band vibrates faster, so its frequency becomes higher. A higher frequency gives a higher pitch, or shriller sound.

items.q: An LED in a tester glows even when a bulb does not glow, because:
options: An LED works with very small currents

items.proposedAnswer: The water breaks down and bubbles of gas form at the electrodes. The gases produced are hydrogen and oxygen.

options: Tin is a poor conductor of sound

items.q: Why are cheaper metal ornaments sometimes coated with gold or silver by electroplating?
items.proposedAnswer: Electroplating gives them the shiny look of the costly metal while using only a thin layer, so they cost less. The coating also protects the cheaper metal from corrosion.
keyPoints: Gives shiny look of costly metal
Only a thin layer needed, so cheaper

items.q: Lightning is caused by:
options: Discharge of electric charges between clouds, or between clouds and the ground

items.q: Earthquakes are caused by:
options: Disturbance deep inside the Earth's crust

items.q: Electric charges are of:
State the rule of attraction and repulsion between electric charges.
items.proposedAnswer: Like charges repel each other and unlike charges attract each other.

items.q: A lightning conductor on a tall building protects it because it:
options: Provides a safe path for the charge to flow to the ground

items.q: A rainbow is formed because:
options: Water droplets in the air disperse sunlight into its colours

items.q: Write three precautions to take during an earthquake if you are indoors.
items.proposedAnswer: Take shelter under a strong table or desk, stay away from windows, glass and heavy objects that may fall, and protect your head. After the shaking stops, go to an open space calmly.
keyPoints: Stay away from windows and heavy objects
Move to an open area after shaking stops

items.q: Which of the following is a cereal crop?
Which of the following is a pulse?
A hoe is a farm tool used for:
options: Removing weeds and loosening the soil

items.q: A combine harvester is a machine that:
options: Harvests the crop and also separates the grain from the husk

items.q: What is irrigation, and why do crops need it?
items.proposedAnswer: Irrigation is the supply of water to crops at regular intervals. Plants need water to absorb nutrients from the soil, and water is also needed for germination, growth and to protect crops from frost and hot air currents.
keyPoints: Supply of water to crops at intervals

items.q: If the same crop is grown in the same field year after year, the soil becomes poor because:
options: The same crop takes up the same nutrients from the soil again and again

items.q: A farmer is about to spray a weedicide in the field. Which precaution is most important?
options: Wear a protective cover over the mouth and nose, and wash hands afterwards
Spray when the wind blows toward him
Taste the liquid to check strength
Spray without any cover to save time

items.q: Why is the soil ploughed and broken into fine pieces before sowing? How do earthworms help?
items.proposedAnswer: Loose soil lets the roots go deep, gets more air and lets roots breathe, and brings nutrient-rich soil to the top. Earthworms and microbes in the soil help to turn and mix the soil and add humus, so the soil stays fertile.
keyPoints: Loose soil helps roots penetrate and breathe
Earthworms and microbes turn the soil and add humus

items.q: Curd is formed from milk by the action of:
Penicillin, the first antibiotic, was discovered by:
Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine against:
Which of the following diseases can spread through contaminated drinking water?
Explain how curd is made at home from milk.
items.proposedAnswer: A little curd, which contains Lactobacillus bacteria, is added to warm milk and left undisturbed for some hours. The bacteria multiply and change the milk into curd.
keyPoints: Add a little curd to warm milk

items.q: Why is it advised to boil drinking water in places where the water supply may be unsafe?
Food is stored in a refrigerator because:
options: Low temperature slows the growth of microorganisms
The refrigerator kills all microbes inside

items.q: Distinguish between a vaccine and an antibiotic.
items.proposedAnswer: A vaccine is given before infection to prepare the body to fight a disease by making antibodies, so it prevents illness. An antibiotic is a medicine given to kill or stop bacteria after a person is infected.
keyPoints: Vaccine prevents disease by making antibodies

items.q: Fibres obtained from plants and animals, such as cotton, wool and silk, are called:
Polythene is commonly used to make:

A polymer is:
options: A small single unit of matter
A large molecule made of many small units joined together

items.q: What do biodegradable and non-biodegradable mean? Give one example of each.
items.proposedAnswer: Biodegradable materials can be broken down by microorganisms into simple substances, for example vegetable waste. Non-biodegradable materials cannot be broken down in this way, for example plastic bags.

items.q: Melamine is used to make kitchenware and fire-resistant fabrics because it:
options: Is a good conductor of heat
Resists heat and does not catch fire easily

items.q: Clothes made of synthetic fibres dry faster than cotton clothes because synthetic fibres:
options: Are heated by the Sun more

items.q: In hot, humid summers, cotton clothes are more comfortable than polyester clothes. Why?
items.proposedAnswer: Cotton absorbs sweat and lets it evaporate, which cools the body. Polyester absorbs very little water, so sweat stays on the skin and the person feels hot and sticky.

items.q: Which of the following non-metals is lustrous (shiny)?
The property of metals by which they can be beaten into thin sheets is called:
Solid non-metals such as sulphur are generally:
Which of the following metals reacts the most vigorously with cold water?
What is a displacement reaction? Give an example involving a metal.
items.proposedAnswer: A displacement reaction is one in which a more reactive metal pushes out a less reactive metal from its salt solution. For example, iron displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.
keyPoints: More reactive metal displaces less reactive metal
From a solution of its salt
Example with iron and copper sulphate

items.q: A dull, grey piece of an old metal object becomes shiny after rubbing with sandpaper. The reason is that:
options: The metal changes into a non-metal
Heat is added to the metal
A dull layer of oxide or tarnish on the surface was rubbed off

items.q: Aluminium foil is used for wrapping food because it:
options: Can be rolled into very thin sheets and does not readily react with food

items.q: Name two ways to prevent iron objects from rusting and explain how one of them works.
items.proposedAnswer: Rusting can be prevented by painting or by oiling and greasing the iron. These coatings keep air and moisture away from the surface, and iron needs both to rust.
keyPoints: Coating keeps out air and moisture
Rusting needs both oxygen and water

items.q: LPG stands for:
Coal is mostly made of:
The slow conversion of dead vegetation into coal over millions of years is called:
What are fossil fuels? Name two.
items.proposedAnswer: Fossil fuels are fuels formed from the remains of dead plants and animals buried under the earth for millions of years. Coal and petroleum are examples.
keyPoints: Formed from dead plants and animals

items.q: In a petroleum refinery, the different products are separated from crude oil on the basis of their different:
Coal and petroleum will not last forever because:
options: They are present only in the sea
The rate at which we use them is much greater than the rate at which they form

items.q: Mention three ways in which a driver can save petrol or diesel.
items.proposedAnswer: A driver can switch off the engine at traffic lights, drive at a steady moderate speed and keep the tyres inflated to the correct pressure. Regular servicing of the vehicle also saves fuel.
keyPoints: Switch off engine at red light

items.q: Which of the following is a feature of an ideal fuel?
options: It is cheap, easily available and burns easily without harmful products
It produces a lot of smoke
It burns only at very high temperatures

items.q: Which of the following is a gaseous fuel?
In a candle flame, the bright yellow middle zone is due to:
options: Partial burning of the fuel, in which tiny unburnt carbon particles glow

items.q: State the three ways of putting out a fire.
items.proposedAnswer: A fire can be put out by cutting off the supply of air (oxygen), removing the fuel, or cooling the fuel below its ignition temperature. For example, water cools the burning material.

items.q: Oil in a frying pan catches fire. What is the safest first action?
options: Cover the pan with a lid

items.q: A gas stove gives more heat than burning the same mass of wood. This is because LPG has:
options: A higher calorific value than wood

items.q: How does burning of fuels contribute to global warming?
items.proposedAnswer: Burning fuels such as coal, petrol and diesel releases carbon dioxide into the air. Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere, so increased amounts raise the temperature of the Earth.

items.q: A large area set aside to conserve wild animals, plants and their habitat, where private activities such as grazing and cultivation are not allowed, is a:
Project Tiger was started to:
options: Protect tigers and their habitats in India

items.q: Which of the following is a cause of extinction of animal species?
Give two reasons why forests are important.
items.proposedAnswer: Forests are home to many plants and animals. They give us wood, medicines and food, prevent soil erosion, and absorb carbon dioxide while releasing oxygen.

items.q: Why is destruction of habitat a major threat to wild animals?
options: They lose their food, shelter and breeding places

items.q: If all the snakes in a field are killed, what is most likely to happen?
options: The number of frogs will not change
The number of rats may increase and damage the crop

items.q: Suggest three ways in which students can help to protect forests and wildlife.
items.proposedAnswer: Students can plant and take care of trees, avoid wasting paper, and refuse to buy products made from wild animals. They can also spread awareness about not littering or disturbing forests.
keyPoints: Do not buy wildlife products or spread awareness

items.q: Which of the following is found only in plant cells?
Cells can be seen with the help of a:
The genes that pass on features from parents to children are present on the:
Write the function of the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
items.proposedAnswer: The nucleus controls all the activities of the cell and holds the chromosomes. The cytoplasm is the jelly-like part in which the organelles lie and where many chemical reactions of the cell take place.
keyPoints: Nucleus controls the cell and holds chromosomes

items.q: A scientist finds that a cell has a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole. The cell most likely came from:
Which statement about the cell membrane is correct?
options: It is present only in plant cells
It is a thick rigid layer outside every cell
It is present in both plant and animal cells and controls what enters and leaves

items.q: What is the function of the large vacuole in a plant cell?
items.proposedAnswer: The vacuole stores water, food and waste substances. It also keeps the cell firm because it is filled with fluid pressing on the cell wall.

items.q: The change of a tadpole into an adult frog is called:
A zygote divides repeatedly and forms a ball of cells called the:
Which of the following animals lays eggs (is oviparous)?
What is the difference between oviparous and viviparous animals? Give one example of each.
items.proposedAnswer: Oviparous animals lay eggs, and the young develop outside the mother's body, for example hens. Viviparous animals give birth to young ones that have developed inside the mother, for example cows or humans.
keyPoints: Viviparous give birth to young ones

items.q: Millions of sperms are released in humans, though only one sperm fertilises an egg. Why?
options: The egg needs many sperms to grow
Many sperms are lost or die on the way, so a large number increases the chance of fertilisation
The body cannot stop producing them

items.q: Which statement about asexual reproduction is correct?
options: It needs both male and female gametes
The offspring look very different from the parent

items.q: Describe how a fertilised egg develops into a baby in humans.
items.proposedAnswer: The zygote divides repeatedly to form an embryo, which gets attached to the wall of the uterus. The embryo develops body parts, and after the stage called foetus the baby is born after about nine months.
keyPoints: Foetus develops and baby is born

items.q: Which of the following is a change in girls during puberty?
The thyroid gland is located in the:
Insulin is produced by the:
What is the difference between primary and secondary sexual characters?
items.proposedAnswer: Primary sexual characters are the sex organs present from birth, such as testes and ovaries. Secondary sexual characters appear at puberty, such as a beard in boys and development of breasts in girls.
keyPoints: Primary: sex organs present from birth

items.q: Why is the use of iodised salt recommended?
options: Iodine in it is needed by the thyroid to make thyroxine and prevents goitre

items.q: Rahul feels moody and irritable during adolescence. What is the most likely explanation?
options: Hormonal changes in the body at this age can affect mood
He is ill with a serious infection
He has a vitamin deficiency only
He has a defect in his eyes

items.q: Why is personal hygiene especially important during adolescence?
items.proposedAnswer: At puberty the sweat glands become more active and the skin becomes oily, which can cause body odour and pimples. Bathing daily, wearing clean clothes and keeping the skin clean prevent infections.

items.q: Which of the following is a type of friction?

The pressure of the atmosphere acts:
Why do deep-sea divers wear special suits?
items.proposedAnswer: Pressure in water increases with depth, so at great depth the pressure on the body is very large. A special suit protects the diver from this high pressure.
keyPoints: Very high pressure at great depth

items.q: When you drink through a straw, the liquid rises because:
options: The liquid is lighter than air
Pressure inside the mouth is reduced, and atmospheric pressure pushes the liquid up

items.q: It is easier to move a heavy load on a cart with wheels than to drag it on the ground because:
options: Rolling friction is much less than sliding friction

items.q: Why do we sprinkle fine powder on a carrom board before playing?
items.proposedAnswer: The powder forms a thin layer between the board and the striker or coins, which reduces friction. The pieces then slide easily and smoothly over the board.

items.q: In the human ear, which part starts vibrating when sound waves strike it?
Sound cannot travel through:
Sounds of frequency higher than 20,000 Hz are called:
Distinguish between music and noise.
items.proposedAnswer: Music is a pleasant sound produced by vibrations that are regular and well arranged. Noise is an unpleasant sound with irregular vibrations.

items.q: A ruler is held on a table with part of it hanging over the edge and plucked. If more of the ruler is slid out over the edge, the sound will have:
A person who puts an ear on a railway track can hear an approaching train before it can be heard through air. This is because:
options: Sound travels faster in solids than in air
The train makes more sound on the track

items.q: Describe the path of sound through the human ear in simple steps.
items.proposedAnswer: Sound waves enter the ear canal from the pinna and make the eardrum vibrate. The vibrations are passed on through the middle ear to the inner ear, and nerves carry the message to the brain.
keyPoints: Sound enters through pinna and ear canal
Nerves carry signals to the brain

items.q: Which of the following does NOT conduct electricity?

options: Provides copper that is deposited on the object

items.proposedAnswer: Electroplating is used to give a shiny, attractive finish to objects such as jewellery and car parts. It is also used to protect metals like iron from rusting, for example by chromium or tin plating.

items.q: A tester bulb does not glow when its ends are dipped in a liquid. Which conclusion is the most reasonable?
options: The liquid is a very strong conductor
The liquid may be a poor conductor, and a more sensitive LED tester can be tried

items.q: Testing a liquid using a cell is safe, but testing it with the household mains supply is dangerous because:
options: A cell has a low voltage, whereas the mains has a high voltage that can give a serious shock

items.q: Why does salt solution conduct electricity while pure distilled water and sugar solution do not?
items.proposedAnswer: Salt dissolves in water to give charged particles that can carry the current through the liquid. Distilled water and sugar solution have no such charged particles, so they do not conduct.
keyPoints: Distilled water and sugar solution lack them

items.q: An object becomes electrically charged when:
options: It is rubbed with another suitable object

items.q: The Earth's crust is made of broken parts called:

A kaleidoscope produces beautiful patterns because of:
How does a periscope help us to see over an obstacle?
items.proposedAnswer: A periscope has two plane mirrors fixed at 45 degrees at its two ends. Light from the object reflects from the top mirror to the lower mirror and then to the eye, so we can see objects over a wall.
keyPoints: Two plane mirrors at the ends

items.q: When white light passes through a prism, which colour bends the most?
A disc painted with the seven rainbow colours is spun very fast. It appears:
We can see our image in a plane mirror but cannot catch it on a screen. Why?
items.proposedAnswer: The image in a plane mirror is virtual. It is formed behind the mirror where light rays only appear to meet, so it cannot be obtained on a screen.

items.q: Which is the first step in the production of a crop?

Write two differences between manure and a chemical fertiliser.
items.proposedAnswer: Manure is made from the decomposition of plant and animal waste, while a fertiliser is a man-made chemical produced in factories. Manure adds humus to the soil but a fertiliser does not, and a fertiliser is richer in particular nutrients.
keyPoints: Manure is natural; fertiliser is man-made
Fertiliser is rich in specific nutrients

items.q: Which practice helps to restore nitrogen in the soil without using a fertiliser?
options: Growing the same cereal every year
Growing a pulse crop in rotation with cereals

items.q: If seeds are sown very close to each other, the result is likely to be:
options: Competition for water, nutrients and light, leading to weak plants

items.q: Why are rabi crops such as wheat sown in winter and kharif crops such as paddy in the rainy season?
items.proposedAnswer: Rabi crops need a cool growing period and little water, so they grow well in winter. Kharif crops need warm weather and plenty of water, which the monsoon rains supply.
keyPoints: Kharif crops need warmth and abundant water
Rains supply water to kharif crops

items.q: Microorganisms are so small that they can be seen only with the help of a:
Which of the following is an alga?
The antibiotic penicillin is obtained from a:
Write two harmful effects of microorganisms.
items.proposedAnswer: Some microorganisms cause diseases in humans, animals and plants, such as cholera and typhoid. Others spoil food, making it unsafe to eat and causing food poisoning.

items.q: Why can eating spoilt food lead to food poisoning?
options: Spoilt food has too many vitamins
Microorganisms growing on it release toxic substances
The food has become too soft
It has lost all its water

items.q: Why is sugar used to preserve jams and squashes?
options: It reduces the moisture, so microorganisms cannot grow

items.q: How can the spread of cholera be prevented in a village?
items.proposedAnswer: The water should be boiled or purified before drinking, and food must be covered and kept clean. People should wash hands before eating, and waste should be disposed of properly so that flies do not carry germs.

items.q: PVC is commonly used to make:
Which of the following fibres is made from petroleum products?
Fishing nets and tyre cords are made of nylon mainly because it has:
Write two uses of nylon.
items.proposedAnswer: Nylon is used to make ropes, fishing nets and parachutes because it is strong and light. It is also used to make toothbrush bristles, socks and tents.
keyPoints: Other items such as toothbrush bristles

items.q: Plastic cooking utensils are not placed on a flame because:
options: They can melt or burn, and spoil the food

items.q: Why is burning plastic waste harmful?
options: It releases poisonous gases into the air

items.q: Plastics are both useful and harmful. Explain with two points each.
items.proposedAnswer: Plastics are useful because they are light, cheap and strong, and they do not rust. They are harmful because they are non-biodegradable and pollute the land and water, and burning them gives poisonous gases.

items.q: Which non-metal present in air is needed by living things for breathing?
Metals are generally:
options: Poor conductors of heat and electricity
Good conductors of heat and electricity

items.q: Oxides of metals are generally:
Why are iron and steel used in building bridges and buildings?
items.proposedAnswer: Iron and steel are very strong and hard and have high melting points. They can be shaped into beams and rods, so they can carry large loads.

items.q: A piece of iron and a piece of sulphur are dropped into separate test tubes of dilute hydrochloric acid. What is observed?
options: Iron reacts and gives off hydrogen, but sulphur does not react

items.q: Mercury is used in some thermometers because it:
options: Is a gas at room temperature
Is a liquid metal at room temperature and expands evenly on heating

items.q: A metal spoon left in a cup of hot tea soon becomes hot. Explain why.
items.proposedAnswer: Metals are good conductors of heat. The heat of the tea passes through the metal spoon by conduction from the hot end to the end held in the hand.
keyPoints: Metals are good conductors of heat

items.q: The hard, porous, black solid obtained by heating coal strongly in the absence of air is called:
The thick, black liquid obtained during the processing of coal is called:
Which gas obtained during processing of coal is used as a fuel in industries near coal processing plants?
Which petroleum product is used as a fuel for heavy vehicles such as trucks and buses?
What is natural gas? Mention two of its uses.
items.proposedAnswer: Natural gas is a fossil fuel found trapped with petroleum, and its main constituent is methane. It is used as a fuel (as CNG in vehicles) and as a starting material for making fertilisers and other chemicals.
keyPoints: Uses such as CNG and chemicals

items.q: LPG is preferred to wood as a domestic fuel mainly because it:
options: Burns with little smoke and has a high calorific value

items.q: A person smells gas in the kitchen and suspects an LPG leak. What should be done first?
options: Switch on the exhaust fan with the electrical switch
Open the windows and doors and avoid using any electrical switch or flame

items.q: What is the difference between renewable and non-renewable resources? Give an example of each.
items.proposedAnswer: Renewable resources can be replaced by nature in a short time, such as sunlight and wind. Non-renewable resources take millions of years to form and will get exhausted, such as coal and petroleum.
keyPoints: Non-renewable: limited and take millions of years

items.q: When a fuel containing carbon burns completely, the main products are:
Which gas supports combustion?
Which of the following is a solid fuel?
Which of these has the highest calorific value?
What is an explosion? Why are firecrackers dangerous?
items.proposedAnswer: An explosion is a sudden reaction in which a large amount of heat, light, sound and gas is produced. Firecrackers can burn the skin, hurt the eyes and ears, cause fires and pollute the air, so they must be used with care.
keyPoints: Sudden reaction with heat, light, sound and gas

items.q: Which of the following actions would reduce air pollution caused by burning fuels?
options: Burning more wood in open fires

items.q: A piece of wood burns slowly, but fine wood shavings burn quickly. The reason is that shavings:
options: Have a larger surface exposed to the air

items.q: How does a carbon dioxide fire extinguisher put out a fire?
items.proposedAnswer: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air, so it covers the burning material like a blanket and cuts off the supply of oxygen. It also cools the fuel as it comes out of the cylinder.
keyPoints: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air
Covers the fire like a blanket

items.q: The variety of plants and animals found in an area is called:
The place where a plant or animal lives naturally is called its:
Large-scale deforestation in a region can reduce its:
The main reasons why many animals migrate are:
options: Better climate, food or a place to breed

items.q: Write the difference between a wildlife sanctuary and a national park.
items.proposedAnswer: In a wildlife sanctuary, animals are protected from hunting, but some human activities may be allowed. A national park is a more strictly protected area in which activities like grazing and cultivation are not allowed.
keyPoints: Some human activity may be allowed in sanctuaries
National park is more strictly protected

items.q: A paper factory needs a lot of wood. Which approach helps to keep forests safe?
options: Cut trees and also plant new saplings (reforestation)
Stop all use of paper only

items.q: Why is it important to conserve biodiversity?
options: All species in an ecosystem depend on one another, so loss of one affects others
Plants are not part of biodiversity
Species do not depend on each other

items.q: Explain how deforestation can lead to a shortage of water or drought in an area.
items.proposedAnswer: Trees take water from the soil and release it into the air, which helps to form rain. Without trees there is less rainfall, and the water runs off the bare soil quickly instead of soaking in, so the area becomes dry.

items.q: The cell wall of plant cells is made of:
The green pigment that traps sunlight is present in:
Which of the following is a multicellular organism?
Which of the following shows the correct order of organisation in a multicellular organism, from simplest to most complex?
Name any three parts of an animal cell and write one function of each.
items.proposedAnswer: The cell membrane controls entry and exit of substances. The nucleus controls the activities of the cell. The cytoplasm holds the organelles and is the place of many reactions.

items.q: A slide of human cheek cells is seen under a microscope. Which of the following would you find?
options: A nucleus and cell membrane but no cell wall

items.q: A plant wilts if it is not watered. The main reason is that its cells:
options: Lose water from the vacuoles and lose their firmness

items.q: An Amoeba is a single cell, yet it is a complete living organism. Explain.
items.proposedAnswer: A single cell of Amoeba carries out all the life processes itself, such as taking in food, respiration, getting rid of waste, movement and reproduction. It does not need other cells for these functions.
keyPoints: One cell performs all life processes

items.q: The male reproductive organ that produces sperms is the:
Reproductive cells (sperms and eggs) are together called:
Which of the following animals shows metamorphosis?
Which of the following shows internal fertilisation?
Name the male reproductive organs and state the functions of the testes.
items.proposedAnswer: The male reproductive system has a pair of testes, sperm ducts and a penis. The testes produce sperms and the male hormone testosterone.

items.q: A hen sits on its eggs for about three weeks. The main purpose is to:
options: Keep the eggs warm so that the embryos can develop into chicks

items.q: Identical twins are formed when:
options: Two different eggs are fertilised by two sperms
A single fertilised egg splits into two embryos

items.q: Why is internal fertilisation more dependable than external fertilisation?
items.proposedAnswer: In internal fertilisation the sperms are released inside the female body, so they are close to the egg and well protected, giving a good chance of fertilisation. Fewer eggs are needed, and the young are often cared for.
keyPoints: Sperms close to egg inside the body

items.q: The sudden rapid increase in height during adolescence is called:
The voice box is also known as the:

Menstruation occurs when:
options: The egg released from the ovary is not fertilised and the lining of the uterus breaks down

items.q: What is menstruation? At what stage of life does it begin and stop?
items.proposedAnswer: Menstruation is the monthly flow of blood and tissue from the uterus when an egg is not fertilised. It begins at puberty and stops around the age of 45 to 50 years.

items.q: The menstrual cycle does not occur in a woman during pregnancy because:
options: The egg that was released was fertilised and the uterus lining is kept for the baby

items.q: Why is it advised to eat iron-rich food such as green leafy vegetables during adolescence?
options: Iron helps make haemoglobin in the blood and prevents anaemia

items.q: Explain why the pituitary gland is important at puberty.
items.proposedAnswer: The pituitary gland releases hormones that make the testes and ovaries start producing sex hormones, and it also releases the hormone for growth. In this way it controls the changes at puberty.

items.q: The force that pulls objects towards the Earth is called:

The pressure on a surface increases when:
options: The same force acts on a smaller area
The same force acts on a bigger area
The force is reduced and the area is the same

items.q: What is atmospheric pressure? Why do we not feel it?
items.proposedAnswer: Atmospheric pressure is the pressure exerted by the air around us. We do not feel it because the pressure of the fluids inside our bodies balances it.

items.q: A person exerts more pressure on the ground when standing on one foot than on both feet because:
options: The area of contact is halved, so the pressure doubles

items.q: Tractors have very wide tyres because:
options: They spread the weight over a larger area and reduce the pressure on the soil

items.q: Why do nails and drawing pins have pointed tips?
items.proposedAnswer: A pointed tip has a very small area, so when force is applied the pressure is large, and the nail easily goes into the wood or board.

items.q: The time taken for one complete vibration is called the:

options: The beat of a bass drum

items.q: What is amplitude? How does it affect the sound we hear?
items.proposedAnswer: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of a vibrating object from its rest position. A larger amplitude produces a louder sound and a smaller amplitude a softer sound.

items.q: An object vibrates 200 times in half a second. What is its frequency?
Which of the following frequencies cannot be heard by a normal human ear?
In a guitar, how can the pitch of the sound from a string be made higher?
items.proposedAnswer: The pitch becomes higher when the string is tightened, shortened or replaced by a thinner string, because it then vibrates with a higher frequency.
keyPoints: Shorten the string or use a thinner one

items.q: Electric current flows in a circuit only when the circuit is:

items.proposedAnswer: A conductor allows electric current to pass through it, for example copper. An insulator does not allow current to pass through, for example rubber.

items.q: When a liquid is placed in a tester circuit, the bulb glows only dimly. This suggests that the liquid is:

options: Water that contains dissolved salts conducts electricity and can cause a shock

items.q: Describe briefly how a spoon can be electroplated with silver.
items.proposedAnswer: The spoon is made the negative electrode (cathode) and a silver plate is the positive electrode (anode) in a solution of a silver salt. When electric current is passed, silver from the solution is deposited on the spoon.
keyPoints: Silver plate is the anode in a silver salt solution
Current deposits silver on the spoon

items.q: In the colours of a rainbow, orange comes immediately after:

items.proposedAnswer: We should stay inside a building or a car and avoid standing under tall trees or in open fields. We should also avoid using electrical appliances and corded phones, and stay away from water.
keyPoints: Stay inside a building or vehicle
Avoid tall trees and open ground

items.q: Which house design would be the safest in an earthquake-prone area?
options: A light building with a strong, flexible frame
A very heavy stone building with no frame
A tall building with heavy objects on the top

items.q: A girl stands 3 m in front of a plane mirror and then walks 1 m toward it. What is the new distance between her and her image?
A balloon is rubbed against hair and then sticks to a wall. Explain why.
items.proposedAnswer: Rubbing charges the balloon with static electricity. When the charged balloon is brought near the wall, it attracts opposite charge on the wall surface, so the balloon is held to it for some time.
keyPoints: Charged object induces opposite charge on the wall

items.q: Which of the following is an oilseed crop?
A sickle is a farm tool used for:
The sprinkler system of irrigation is most useful for:
options: Uneven land where water is scarce

items.q: Fertilisers are added to the soil mainly to:
options: Replace the nutrients that earlier crops have taken
Increase the number of earthworms only

items.q: What is threshing, and how is it done on large farms?
items.proposedAnswer: Threshing is the separation of grain seeds from the dry stalks and husk of the harvested crop. On large farms it is done with a machine called a combine harvester, which also harvests the crop.
keyPoints: Separating grain from stalks and husk

items.q: A field has become less fertile after chemical fertilisers have been used alone for many years. What is the best remedy?
options: Add more of the same fertiliser
Add manure and rotate the crops

items.q: Weeds should be removed from a crop field early because weeds:
options: Compete with the crop for nutrients, water and light, and may harbour pests

items.q: Why do seeds need water in order to germinate?
items.proposedAnswer: Seeds take in water, which softens the seed coat and wakes up the embryo inside. The water also helps the stored food to be used by the growing seedling.
keyPoints: Stored food is used by the seedling

items.q: Which of the following is a protozoan?
Medicines that kill or stop the growth of bacteria are called:
Yeast is used in the commercial production of:
Dengue is spread by the:
Name three methods of preserving food at home and say how each works.
items.proposedAnswer: Heating or cooking and refrigeration keep microbes from growing. Salting and adding sugar remove water, and adding oil or vinegar in pickles keeps air and microbes away.

items.q: Sodium benzoate is added to jams and squashes in small amounts to:
Why are children given vaccines at an early age?
options: To prepare their body to fight diseases before they get infected
To cure a disease they already have

items.q: Why is it important to wash hands with soap before eating?
items.proposedAnswer: Our hands pick up microbes from the surroundings. Washing with soap removes them, so they do not enter the body with the food and cause diseases such as diarrhoea.

items.q: Fibres that are made from chemical substances in factories are called:
Which plastic is used to coat non-stick cookware?
Which statement about polyester fabric is correct?
options: It absorbs a lot of water
It is made from a plant
It is heavy and always crumples
It is wrinkle-resistant and easy to wash

items.q: What is PET and what is it used for?
items.proposedAnswer: PET (polyethylene terephthalate) is a plastic that is light, strong and clear. It is used to make bottles and containers for drinks and food.

items.q: Shirts are often made from a blend of cotton and polyester because the blend:
options: Combines the comfort of cotton with the wrinkle resistance of polyester

items.q: Which of the following habits helps to reduce plastic pollution?
options: Using a new plastic bag every time

items.q: How are synthetic fibres different from natural fibres in their source and properties?
items.proposedAnswer: Natural fibres such as cotton and wool come from plants and animals, whereas synthetic fibres such as nylon are made from chemicals in factories. Synthetic fibres are usually stronger, dry quickly and last longer, but they melt and catch fire easily.
keyPoints: Synthetic are strong, durable and quick drying but melt easily

items.q: Which of the following metals is commonly used to make jewellery?
Which of the following is a metal?
When carbon burns in air, the gas produced is:
Write two differences between metals and non-metals.
items.proposedAnswer: Metals are generally lustrous, malleable, ductile and good conductors of heat and electricity. Non-metals are generally dull, brittle if solid, and poor conductors of heat and electricity.
keyPoints: Metals are lustrous, malleable and ductile
Non-metals are dull, brittle and poor conductors

items.q: A student tries to bend a copper wire and a piece of coal. The wire bends but the coal breaks. This shows that:
options: Metals are ductile and malleable, whereas coal is brittle

items.q: A silver spoon left in the air for a long time becomes dark because:
options: It reacts with substances such as sulphur compounds in the air
The spoon gets heated by sunlight

items.q: Why are the handles of cooking pans made of plastic or wood instead of metal?
items.proposedAnswer: Metals are good conductors of heat, so a metal handle would become too hot to hold. Plastic and wood are poor conductors, so the handle remains cool enough to hold.
keyPoints: Plastic and wood are poor conductors

items.q: Petrol, diesel and kerosene are obtained from:
Coal is a:
Which coal product is used for making naphthalene balls, dyes and paints?
State two uses of coal.
items.proposedAnswer: Coal is used as a fuel in homes, in industries and in power plants to generate electricity. Its product, coke, is used in making steel.

items.q: Compared with petrol, vehicles that run on CNG:
In an oil-bearing rock, natural gas is found above the petroleum. This is because natural gas is:
Why are coal and petroleum called fossil fuels?
items.proposedAnswer: They were formed from the remains of dead plants and animals, which were buried under the earth for millions of years. Heat and pressure turned them into fuels, as fossils form from old remains.
keyPoints: Formed from remains of dead organisms

items.q: The lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire is called its:
Which of the following catches fire very easily?
Water is a suitable extinguisher for burning wood and paper because it:
options: Cools the material below its ignition temperature

items.q: Distinguish between combustible and non-combustible substances with two examples of each.
items.proposedAnswer: Combustible substances burn in air, such as wood and paper. Non-combustible substances do not burn, such as glass and stone.

items.q: Carbon monoxide, produced in incomplete combustion, is dangerous because it:
options: Is a poisonous gas that has no colour or smell

items.q: Why can sand be used to put out a small fire?
options: It cuts off the supply of air and covers the burning material

items.q: What is calorific value? Why is it important when we choose a fuel?
items.proposedAnswer: Calorific value is the amount of heat produced by the complete burning of 1 kg of a fuel, measured in kJ/kg. A fuel with a higher calorific value gives more heat for the same mass, so it is more efficient.
keyPoints: Heat from complete burning of 1 kg
Higher value means a better fuel

items.q: The plants and animals of a region are together called its:
Cutting down trees to get land for farming or buildings is called:
Animals that move from one region to another according to the season are called:
What is the Red Data Book and why is it important?
items.proposedAnswer: The Red Data Book is a record of species of plants and animals that are endangered or threatened with extinction. It helps in planning how to protect them.

items.q: Which activity damages life in rivers and ponds the most?
options: Dumping industrial waste into the water

items.q: Why should we avoid buying articles made from animal skin or ivory?
options: Demand for them leads to poaching, which endangers species

items.q: How can saving paper help to save forests?
items.proposedAnswer: Paper is made from wood pulp, which comes from trees. If we use less paper and reuse or recycle it, fewer trees are cut, so forests are protected.
keyPoints: Saving paper means fewer trees cut

items.q: The part of a plant cell that lies outside the cell membrane is the:
The genetic information of the cell is stored in the:
Compared with an animal cell, a mature plant cell typically has:
What are cell organelles? Name two of them.
items.proposedAnswer: Organelles are small structures within a cell, each doing a particular job. Two examples are the nucleus and the mitochondria.

items.q: An animal cell cannot make its own food by photosynthesis because it:
Cells in the roots of a plant have no chloroplasts. The most likely reason is that:
options: Sunlight does not reach the roots, so they do not carry out photosynthesis

items.q: Why is the nucleus called the control centre of a cell?
items.proposedAnswer: The nucleus holds the chromosomes with genes, which carry instructions for the cell, so it controls growth, activities and reproduction of the cell. A cell without its nucleus cannot work properly for long.
keyPoints: Controls the activities of the cell
Needed for the cell to function

items.q: The type of reproduction in which two parents are involved is called:
The cell formed by fusion of a sperm and an egg is the:
The stage of development in humans in which all the body parts can be identified is the:
Write two differences between sexual and asexual reproduction.
items.proposedAnswer: In sexual reproduction two parents are involved and gametes fuse, so the young are different from the parents. In asexual reproduction only one parent is involved and the young are almost identical to the parent, as in Hydra budding.
keyPoints: Sexual needs two parents; asexual needs one
Asexual offspring are similar to the parent

items.q: Frogs usually lay their eggs in water in the rainy season because:
options: Tadpoles need water to live and breathe through gills

items.q: Which statement about a zygote is correct?
options: It has only the mother's genes
It is formed by fusion of a sperm and an egg and has genes from both parents

items.q: Why does a child look like both parents?
items.proposedAnswer: The zygote is formed by fusion of a sperm from the father and an egg from the mother, so it gets genes from both. These genes decide the features of the child.
keyPoints: Zygote from father's sperm and mother's egg

What is goitre and how can it be prevented?
items.proposedAnswer: Goitre is a swelling in the neck caused by a lack of iodine, which the thyroid gland needs to make thyroxine. It can be prevented by using iodised salt and eating iodine-rich food.
keyPoints: Swelling of the thyroid gland in the neck

items.q: A teenager develops pimples on the face. What is the best advice?
options: Wash the face regularly with clean water and avoid squeezing the pimples

items.q: When a girl has her first menstrual period, it generally means that:
options: She has reached puberty and her body is maturing for reproduction
She has become an adult in all ways

items.q: Why should adolescents stay away from tobacco, alcohol and drugs?
items.proposedAnswer: These substances harm the body and the brain, especially during the growing years. They can become a habit that is hard to break and cause diseases and problems in studies and life.

items.q: Which example shows a force changing the shape of an object?
options: A ball rolling on the ground

options: The shape of the object only
The roughness of the surfaces and the force pressing them together

items.q: A lubricant reduces friction because it:
options: Forms a thin layer between the surfaces
Increases the force pressing on them

items.q: What is the difference between contact forces and non-contact forces? Give one example of each.
items.proposedAnswer: A contact force acts only when objects touch each other, such as muscular force or friction. A non-contact force acts without touching, such as gravity or the force of a magnet.

items.q: A car skids on a wet road because:
options: A film of water reduces the friction between the tyres and the road

items.q: A glass is filled with water and covered with a card. When it is turned upside down, the card stays in place because:
options: Atmospheric pressure pushes the card upward

items.q: Explain how the brakes of a bicycle stop it.
items.proposedAnswer: When the brake lever is pressed, the brake pads press against the rim of the wheel. The friction between the pads and the rim opposes the motion and slows the wheel until it stops.
keyPoints: Brake pads press on the wheel rim

items.q: Sound travels through air in the form of:

The sound that is heard after reflection from a surface
